doc.title: Bob Havens interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997

title: Discovering Dixieland in New Orleans with George Girard and Al Hirt
summary: Sitting in on Bourbon Street, an offer from George Girard's New Orleans Five, and later the front line of Al Hirt's band with Pete Fountain.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Yeah. Here I’ve only been with Flanagan one month and now I’m on Bourbon Street and I get another offer, and it took me about ten seconds to decide I’d rather play Dixieland than the big band. I finished the tour with Flanagan and four months later I came back to New Orleans and played with George’s band. And I was in New Orleans for five years. And I played with George and after a year or two I switched over to Al Hirt’s jazz band. And Al had started a band. Of course you know in later years he became a big name in the music business. But he and Pete Fountain and I were the original members of the front line of this band in 1957. As you know, Pete Fountain has his own band in New Orleans and is doing very well, and Al is still playing in Bourbon Street and has done
awfully well in his career, and so I got my start in New Orleans. I call it my apprenticeship in jazz.
